sentences.text:
Before
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Anuradha Shukla

On The 6 th Of March, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 1940 of 2005
 Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd
 Versus
 Smt.Sevantabai & Anr
 Appearance:
 Shri Vk.Pandey - Advocate for the appellant.
None for the respondents, though duly served.

A short question involved in this Misc. Appeal is, whether the First Additional Member to Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (for short 'the Tribunal'), Waraseoni, District Balaghat was justified in holding in its award dated 26.02.2005 passed in M.A.C.C. No. 8/2003 that appellant/Insurance Company shall be liable for the compensation for the damage caused to the tractor of respondent No.1/ Insured owner in a railway accident.
2. The claim was that the tractor of respondent No.1 was hit by a train on an unmanned railway crossing, which was not closed when the train was passing by.
Claiming that the tractor was insured with appellant/Insurance Company, a claim petition for a compensation of 3, 47,641/- was filed.

The Tribunal allowed it to the extent of 1,47,641/-qua appellant/Insurance Company, while the second NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18054 2 MA-1940-2005 respondent, namely,
Manager Southeast Railways, Nagpur was discharged of any liabilities.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present appeal has been preferred on the grounds that under the provision of Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988, a claim can be preferred by a third-party or the owner of third-party property, but in the instant case, the claimant/respondent No.1 was the first party as she was the owner of the damaged property and was claiming compensation against her own Insurance Company.

According to appellant a grave error was committed by Tribunal in allowing the claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, while there exists a separate forum under Consumer Protection Act for dealing with the cases of own damage.

It is further submitted that not only the property damage claim could have been filed by a third-party alone but that could have been allowed only to an extent of 6000/- under the contractual liability.
Thus, a prayer is made to set aside the impugned award.
4. Counsel for the appellant has been heard on the merits of the case while none appeared on behalf of respondents.
Record of the Tribunal has been perused.
5. From the nature and the contents of the claim petition, it appears that the same was filed under misconceived notions of law.

If it was a case of untoward Railway accident, the claim should have been preferred before the Railways Claims Tribunal, and if the accident was caused on account of negligence of the driver of respondent No.1/ owner of tractor, the claim should have been preferred under the own damages clause of the Insurance Policy which would not lie before Motor Accident Claims Tribunal under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Thus, on both aspects the claim petition was untenable under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.

The Tribunal discharged Railways of any liability by holding that there was no negligence on its part in the commission of accident, but Tribunal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18054 3 MA-1940-2005 ignored the fact that for the negligence of her own driver, respondent No.1- claimant was not entitled to any compensation under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.

In support of aforesaid legal proposition,
reliance has been duly placed by counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited versus Lakshmi Narayan Dhut, (2007) 3 SCC 700.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited versus Lakshmi Narayan Dhut, (2007) 3 SCC 700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further in the case of Ram Khiladi and another versus United India Insurance Company and another, (2020) 2 SCC 550, the Apex Court has held that a claim of owner/
insured even under section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act is not maintainable against the Insurance Company of the vehicle involved in the accident and such a damage case will be covered only under the own damage clause if the insurance policy permits so.
6.

entities.text: Ram Khiladi and another versus United India Insurance Company and another, (2020) 2 SCC 550
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In terms aforesaid settled legal position and the facts of the case, this appeal is allowed and it is held that respondent No.1-claimant, who was also the owner/ insured of the damaged vehicle is not entitled to claim any compensation under the provision of Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against Insurance Company of the vehicle involved in the accident, the appellant here.
The impugned award is, in consequence, set aside and appeal is disposed of.

7. Let a copy of this order along with record be send back to the concerned Tribunal for information and necessary compliance.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE skt Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd vs Smt.Sevantabai & Anr on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175116979/
